title: Wyoming Stable Token Commission Moves FRNT Infrastructure To Chainlink CCIP
summary: Wyoming Stable Token Commission Moves FRNT Infrastructure To Chainlink CCIP - Read the full analysis.
content:
The Wyoming Stable Token Commission has migrated its sovereign Frontier Stable Token (FRNT) to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP).
The state entity fully deprecated its previous integration with LayerZero following a security review that raised operational and disclosure concerns.
As the first public-entity stablecoin in the U.S., FRNT leverages CCIP to maintain secure cross-chain functionality across eight major blockchain networks.

Commission leadership stated that CCIP was the only infrastructure capable of satisfying Wyoming's strict security and institutional compliance standards.

The multi-year partnership secures state-backed digital asset transfers while preserving reserve yield generated for Wyoming’s public education fund.

title: Hawkish RBI minutes spark volatility in India’s bond market
summary:

The post Hawkish RBI minutes spark volatility in India’s bond market appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Indian government bond yields spiked after hawkish Reserve Bank of India (RBI) minutes revealed MPC members are prepared to raise interest rates if inflation pressures broaden.


Benchmark 10-year yields surged to a two-month high of 6.87% as heavy selling pressure swept sovereign debt markets.
Policymakers cited persistent food and fuel price volatility alongside rising raw material costs as key catalysts for potential monetary tightening.
The sell-off was further exacerbated by rising global crude oil prices, prompting swap markets to quickly price in rate hike risks for late 2026.
The unexpected shift in central bank tone has shattered expectations for an extended pause, triggering heightened volatility across domestic fixed-income assets.

title: Asian currencies rise as US bond buyback plan faces skepticism: WSJ
summary:

The post Asian currencies rise as US bond buyback plan faces skepticism: WSJ appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Asian currencies gained ground against the U.S. dollar as global markets grew skeptical of Washington’s expanded debt-buyback plan.

The U.S. Treasury Department moved to double its weekly bond repurchases in an attempt to cap surging long-term borrowing costs.
However, an initial drop in Treasury yields quickly reversed as bond investors concluded buybacks offer only temporary liquidity rather than deficit reduction.

The fading impact of the Treasury intervention pulled the U.S. Dollar Index lower, opening space for regional currencies to bounce back.
Analysts warn that unless structural fiscal concerns are resolved, persistent weakness in the greenback will keep Asian exchange rates elevated.

title: Brazil invests $444M to enhance AI ecosystem and supercomputing
summary:
Brazil's AI investment aims to boost technological sovereignty, reduce reliance on foreign tech, and position itself as a global AI leader.
The post Brazil invests $444M to enhance AI ecosystem and supercomputing appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Brazil’s government has committed 2.3 billion reais ($444 million) from its national science fund to accelerate domestic AI and supercomputing capabilities.
The plan allocates $251 million toward a Rio de Janeiro facility partnering with Chinese firms Huawei and iFlytek to train localized language models.
An additional $193 million is earmarked for an AI supercomputing cluster in Rio Grande do Norte designed to rank among the world's top ten.

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva framed the investment as a strategic push toward data sovereignty and domestic infrastructure autonomy.

By balancing procurement between American hardware providers and Chinese tech firms, Brazil aims to build computing power without relying on a single foreign superpower.

title: TerraPay and TPBank Link Up for Real-Time Cross-Border Payments
summary:
Vietnam's TPBank will use TerraPay's 156-country network to offer real-time outbound international payments without building bilateral banking relationships.
The post TerraPay and TPBank Link Up for Real-Time Cross-Border Payments appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content:
Global infrastructure provider TerraPay has partnered with Vietnam’s TPBank to enable real-time cross-border transfers across more than 150 countries.
Through a single API integration, TPBank connects directly to TerraPay’s network, avoiding the complexity of negotiating individual correspondent banking relationships.
The collaboration supports two-way, direct account-to-account and account-to-wallet transactions, eliminating traditional intermediary bank delays.

All international transactions under the agreement remain fully compliant with the State Bank of Vietnam’s foreign exchange and anti-money laundering regulations.
The expansion targets Vietnam's surging digital payment market, connecting local customers to major remittance corridors across Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

title: Cardano Foundation Drafts Dijkstra Upgrade For Smart Contract Execution
summary: Cardano Foundation Drafts Dijkstra Upgrade For Smart Contract Execution - Read the full analysis.
content:
Cardano governance organization Intersect has outlined a two-phase roadmap for its long-awaited Dijkstra upgrade.

Phase one, targeted for Q4 2026, introduces Linear Leios and Plutus V4 to dramatically scale smart contract processing capabilities.
Phase two will follow in Q2 2027, activating Ouroboros Peras via a hard fork to accelerate overall transaction finality.

The phased rollout strategy aims to minimize technical execution risks while allowing thorough testing on preview networks.
Once fully deployed, the enhanced execution architecture is expected to boost ecosystem scalability and layer-1 competitiveness.

title: Capital.com to Offer Spot Virtual-Asset Services in the UAE After Capital Vault Secures Full CMA Licence
summary:
Capital.com today announced plans to offer virtual-asset investment services to clients in the UAE. The move follows a licence granted to its affiliate, Capital Vault Virtual Services L.L.C - S.P.C. (“Capital Vault UAE”), by the Capital Market Authority (CMA), the federal regulator for virtual assets in the UAE.
The licence allows Capital Vault UAE to deal in virtual assets, either as an agent or as a matching principal, and to provide custody for virtual assets on behalf of clients. Capital Vault UAE is among the first firms licensed under the CMA's virtual-asset framework, and the services it supports will be available to Capital.com clients in the UAE.
Once live, Capital.com clients in the UAE will be able to buy virtual-assets outright through the Capital.com app and held in accordance with the client-asset rules applicable to a CMA-licensed custodian. Capital Vault provides that regulated layer, including execution, custody and settlement, under its licence, and operates from an office in Abu Dhabi. This follows Capital Vault Europe which was one of the first batch of firms authorised under MiCA’s CASP framework in December 2025.
Capital Vault operates as a separate regulated entity, focused specifically on virtual assets, with its governance, custody and risk arrangements held separately from Capital.com's other regulated businesses. 
Commenting on the licence, Rahul Kumar, Chief Executive Officer, Capital Vault UAE, said:
“The UAE is at the forefront of virtual-asset regulation in the region, and the Capital Market Authority's review process for virtual-asset licensing reflects that rigour. We have established an office in Abu Dhabi and are building a local team dedicated to virtual assets, and our presence in the UAE is pivotal to our business.”
Commenting on the licence, Tarik Chebib, Chief Executive Officer MENA, Capital.com, said:
“Capital.com clients across the region have been asking for a straightforward, regulated way to buy and hold virtual-assets alongside the markets they already trade. This licence lets us bring that to clients in the UAE, with Capital Vault providing the infrastructure behind it, and more products to follow.”
Additional virtual-asset products will be announced in due course.This approach is built around giving clients a considered way to access digital assets, structured and well-governed. Capital Vault expects to expand its regulatory footprint and its client-facing virtual-asset services in the UAE.
NoYesAsset Management21 Aug, 2026
content: Capital.com plans to offer spot virtual-asset services in the UAE after its affiliate, Capital Vault Virtual Services, secured a full licence from the Capital Market Authority. The regulatory approval enables the firm to provide virtual-asset dealing and custody services to clients in the region, operating through a dedicated office in Abu Dhabi. Additional products are expected to be rolled out as part of the expansion.

title: ZBD Unveils Embedded Financial Infrastructure for Video Games
summary:
ZBD, the money layer for games, today introduces a full platform of embedded financial infrastructure that powers the money lifecycle in games: money in, money through, and money out. The pioneering technology enables money to flow into games, move through them as users earn and transact, and be paid out to players and creators in exchange for the value they create, equipping ZBD to cater fully to PC and console titles following its extensive success in mobile games. 
The financial infrastructure around games is fragmented and unsuited to the way play has evolved. Game economies now routinely need to serve creators, player-to-player commerce, and support esports prizes inside the game. However, existing payment stacks are often retrofitted from other industries, meaning they aren’t built to cater to gaming’s unique use cases and only facilitate one-way transactions. The ability to build a new two-way financial relationship with players means money movement in games evolves from being a cost center to a driver of engagement, revenue, and loyalty.
ZBD has been working to address this problem since 2019 when it set out to develop the tech and secure the licenses to power a complete, embedded payment stack for games. ZBD has raised $90M from investors including RAINE, Square Enix, and Lakestar, and is a licensed payment provider in a majority of US states and across the European Economic Area (EEA). Its rewards and payments technology has been extensively proven in the mobile games industry, where millions of players have engaged with ZBD tech in hundreds of games including Idle Bank from TapNation. Now, the rollout of its complete payment product suite means it can cater to the entire games industry end-to-end.
The ZBD platform encompasses:
Embedded Accounts: ZBD's programmable financial infrastructure layer for studios and publishers integrates licensed embedded accounts for players directly inside a game. Primarily for PC & console platforms, Embedded Accounts enables direct pay-in deposits, real-money P2P marketplaces that reduce gray-market demand, creator economies, and compliant cash-out through licensed payment rails. ZBD Embedded Accounts is an end-to-end financial layer natively integrated into the game. The integration provides publishers with full control over their real-money economy and the financial relationships with players, allowing them to drive deeper player engagement and monetization while enabling new business models never before possible.
Embedded Payouts: Purpose-built for game publishers that need to pay players, creators, and esports competitors at the speed and scale of modern gaming. ZBD Embedded Payouts enables instant, embedded, and compliant cash-out through modern rails including bank accounts, Cash App, gift cards, and push-to-card. It is a single integration layer embedded directly in-game, meaning from KYC to cash out, players never need to leave the game for a third-party payout platform, giving studios the flexibility to build stronger engagement programs for both players and creators.
Embedded Rewards: The next evolution of rewarded play, lifting retention and lifetime value by integrating real-money rewards natively into core gameplay, progression milestones, and LiveOps events. ZBD Embedded Rewards keeps the entire reward journey and cash-out within the game experience, allowing studios to fully own player loyalty for every user. The reward infrastructure layers on top of the game’s existing economy and monetization mechanics, with full compliance and fraud protection handled end-to-end. 
Branded Debit Cards: Built for studios who want to extend player loyalty beyond the game ecosystem, ZBD powers fully configurable white-label debit cards with “cash-back” like rewards that enable players to earn in-game currency or other in-game benefits, such as discounted subscriptions, through real-world purchases. This turns everyday spending on gas and groceries into a continuous loyalty loop that drives player engagement and repeat in-game spending. ZBD fully manages card infrastructure, virtual currency conversion, and compliance. 
Gordon Thornton, CCO at ZBD, said:
“Money has been part of the video games experience for as long as I can remember, but the big shift is that consumers now expect two-way financial relationships with publishers. Studios can now evolve their financial interactions with players, turning a one-way relationship into a two-way loop that drives engagement, revenue, and loyalty. Ultimately, I see our role as enabling studios to implement strategies they’ve always wanted to, but simply haven’t had the tech or licenses available before. This announcement is the culmination of a seven-year mission to build this capability for the industry, and we’re thrilled to already see a lot of pent-up demand from studios and publishers.”
Game developers worldwide have already adopted ZBD’s new embedded technology. 1047 Games, developer of Splitgate and Empulse, is using ZBD’s Embedded Payout technology to power their real-money referral feature and reward players for community-driven growth, while cross-platform publisher Joygame has recently introduced ZBD Embedded Rewards. They join a growing roster of game publishers including TapNation, Udo Games, and Turborilla actively partnering with ZBD to create a two-way value exchange to drive further user retention and loyalty.
John Wright, CEO at Turborilla, said:
“Retention is critical for games to succeed today, and game publishers need to start looking beyond legacy growth playbooks to boost LTV and long-term profitability. ZBD is one of the few companies building for that future by weaving together payments and player engagement. We’re excited to be working with them to bring new loyalty mechanics inside our game, giving our whole player base real value for logging in every day.” 
Unlike traditional payment solutions, ZBD powers the financial infrastructure at the speed and scale games require: on-demand processing, micro-payouts at fractions of a cent, with built-in compliance and fraud protections. ZBD is the only fintech company that combines gaming-native infrastructure, programmable money flows, and compliance rigor into a single licensed layer. 
NoYesInfrastructure21 Aug, 2026
content: ZBD has introduced a comprehensive embedded financial infrastructure platform designed for video games, expanding its services from mobile to PC and console titles. The platform manages the entire money lifecycle in games, featuring embedded accounts, payouts, rewards, and branded debit cards. title: Upbit trading volume spikes 273% as South Korean investors re-enter crypto
summary: One analyst said South Korean capital is slowly moving back to crypto, as investors are 'return-chasing' rather than 'asset-loyal.'
content:

The sharp liquidity influx was largely driven by a wave of new token listings alongside a broader global market rally.
Data shows local traders are rapidly shifting back into speculative altcoin pairs, aiming to capture short-term momentum and outsized returns.
The sudden spike in trading activity pushed South Korea’s "Kimchi Premium" higher, reflecting strong domestic buying pressure relative to global price averages.
The volume surge solidifies Upbit’s market dominance in the region, reaffirming South Korea as one of the world's most active retail crypto hubs.

title: Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins key approval to offer crypto services in Japan
summary:
Japan's crypto market maturity accelerates, attracting institutional interest and necessitating robust infrastructure and trusted services.
The post Nomura-backed Laser Digital wins key approval to offer crypto services in Japan appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content:
Laser Digital, the digital-asset subsidiary of Nomura Holdings, has officially completed its registration as a crypto asset exchange operator in Japan.
The regulatory clearance from the Kanto Local Finance Bureau permits the firm to offer institutional trading and asset brokerage services.
The expansion aims to tap into growing domestic demand as Japanese institutional interest in digital asset allocation reaches record levels.
Alongside trading, Laser Digital is partnering with local entities to explore Japanese yen and U.S. dollar stablecoin issuance.
The milestone reinforces Nomura’s strategy to build a globally regulated crypto infrastructure across Asia, Europe, and the U.S.
